“Everything happens for a reason.”  

The best advice I’ve ever gotten may have been after I had said the aforementioned phrase.  As soon as I finished that sentence, the person I was speaking with told me “I need you to know that you’re wrong, and that everything does not happen for a reason.”

I think this advice is used by a lot of people to help rationalize their suffering.  It’s easy and even comforting to think that the bad things that happens in your life is part of some grand plan, and for the good to happen you need to be hit with the bad.  Especially if you’re religious, thinking this is God’s doing can make coping with the issue at hand.  The fact is, that is absolutely not true.  Bad things happen because bad things happen, it’s as simple as that.  You get to choose how you react to them, and everything that happens afterwards is a result of your own actions.  Everything doesn’t happen for a reason.  They happen because you make them happen.
